answer:
I counted incidents by point-in-polygon matching and calculated:

\[
\text{Rate per 1,000 residents}=\frac{\text{incidents}}{\text{population}}\times 1{,}000
\]

| Zone | Population | Incidents | Rate per 1,000 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Z1 | 5,200 | 41 | 7.885 |
| **Z2** | **830** | **19** | **22.892** |
| Z3 | 4,100 | 22 | 5.366 |
| Z4 | 2,600 | 18 | 6.923 |
| Z5 | 7,400 | 66 | 8.919 |
| Z6 | 3,900 | 25 | 6.410 |
| Z7 | 1,500 | 9 | 6.000 |
| Z8 | 6,100 | 37 | 6.066 |
| Z9 | 2,800 | 14 | 5.000 |

**Zone Z2 has the highest rate: 22.892 incidents per 1,000 residents**, based on 19 incidents among 830 residents.

Of the 256 total incidents, 251 fell within a supplied zone polygon; 5 were outside the zones.
